documents.title: Wave Battle

theme.title: Wave Battle
theme.story: Pirates have hidden their fleet in the bay. Every wave word you know earns a cannon shot. Sink their ships before they sink yours!

documents.directions: Use your waves vocabulary list if you get stuck, then try again without it.

questions.prompt: The distance from one crest of a wave to the next crest is its ___.
questions.why: Wavelength is the length of one full wave, crest to crest (or trough to trough).

questions.prompt: The number of waves that pass a point each second is the wave’s ___.
questions.why: Frequency counts waves per second; it is measured in hertz (Hz).

questions.prompt: The height of a wave from its resting position to a crest is its ___.
questions.why: Amplitude is how far the wave moves from rest. A bigger amplitude means more energy.

questions.prompt: What is the lowest point of a transverse wave called?
questions.why: The highest point is the crest; the lowest point is the trough.

questions.prompt: The material a mechanical wave travels through is called the ___.
questions.why: A medium is the matter a wave moves through, like air for sound or water for ocean waves. A vacuum has no matter at all.

questions.prompt: True or false: sound waves can travel through a vacuum, like outer space.
questions.why: Sound is a mechanical wave: it needs particles to pass the vibration along, and a vacuum has none.

questions.prompt: Which kind of wave can travel through empty space?
questions.why: Light is an electromagnetic wave, which needs no medium. Sound, ocean and rope waves are mechanical waves.

questions.prompt: In a longitudinal wave, the particles of the medium move ___.
choices: up and down, at right angles to the direction the wave travels
in circles, the way a floating cork bobs
back and forth along the direction the wave travels
forward with the wave, all the way to the end
questions.why: In a longitudinal wave (like sound), particles push and pull back and forth in the same direction the wave moves. Up and down is a transverse wave.

questions.prompt: What do we call a wave that needs a medium to travel, like sound?
questions.why: Mechanical waves (sound, water waves, waves on a rope) need matter to travel through.

questions.prompt: True or false: radio waves and visible light are both electromagnetic waves.
questions.why: Radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays are all electromagnetic waves.

questions.prompt: True or false: a wave carries energy from place to place, but it does not carry the medium along with it.
questions.why: A floating leaf bobs up and down as a wave passes but stays in about the same place: the energy moves on, the water doesn’t.

questions.prompt: When a wave bounces off a surface, it is called ___.
questions.why: Reflection is bouncing back, like an echo or a mirror image. Refraction is bending, absorption is soaking up, transmission is passing through.

questions.prompt: A sound gets louder but its pitch stays the same. What changed?
questions.why: Loudness depends on amplitude. Pitch depends on frequency, so if the pitch stays the same, the frequency and wavelength didn’t change.

questions.prompt: Light bends as it passes from air into water. Why?
choices: water absorbs all colors except blue
the light reflects off the water’s surface
the light’s frequency doubles in water
the light’s speed changes in the new medium
questions.why: Refraction happens because light slows down in water. The change in speed bends the light at the boundary.

questions.prompt: Wave A and wave B travel at the same speed. Wave A has a higher frequency. Compared with wave B, wave A has a ___.
questions.why: Speed = frequency × wavelength. At the same speed, a higher frequency means a shorter wavelength.

questions.prompt: Light with a higher frequency than violet light, which can cause sunburn, is called ___ light.
questions.why: Ultraviolet (UV) light is just past violet on the spectrum, with a higher frequency and more energy. It causes sunburn.
